notes:
AE: Priya Shah. SE: Marcus Liu. Mid-market SaaS (B2B chat platform) evaluating Redwood for chat/agent workloads.
- Interested in starting with Hosted API to validate latency/quality in prod traffic, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation.
- Primary workload: multi-tool support-agent that does streaming responses + tool calling (calendar/invoice lookup, KB search). Live chat use during business hours with bursty peaks.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for token streaming start, 99th target <= 400-500ms for end-to-end agent response (customer expects near realtime). Cost sensitive but willing to pay for consistent p95/p99.
- Quality gating: must run prompt/evals regression checks on every model/prompt change. Want automated A/B + canary rollouts with eval-based rollback if QA regressions exceed thresholds.
- Quote from VP Eng: "We need confidence that new prompts/models won't regress customer-facing flows — gating is a hard requirement."
- POC: run seeded portion of traffic (5-10%) through Redwood hosted endpoints, compare latency and conversation quality vs current infra. If meets SLO and eval gates, pilot Dedicated with reserved capacity.
- Security: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS for keys, data residency for EU customers. Sent security questionnaire 2026-02-12 (SEC-1930).
- Pricing: asked for 12-mo TCV scenarios (conservative and optimistic). Interested in burst capacity terms.
- Practical notes: some prompts are long (system + tool call traces) — need prefix/KV caching and efficient batching to hit cost/latency targets.
- Next: Marcus to share POC dataset and latency benchmarks; Priya to send Dedicated pricing scenarios and SLA language.
